title: Canonical module open-square restriction mates and section coprojection
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For every scheme $T$, use the pulled-back ring $\Lambda_T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], its internal module category $\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and its ordinary unbounded derived category $D_T$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], with the size convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Use the module functors, adjunctions, and canonical pullback composition comparisons of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. For arbitrary schemes $X,Y,X',Y'$ and maps $f:X\to Y$, $j:Y'\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $i:X'\to X$ with $f i=j f'$, define the canonical comparison $\chi:f'^*j^*\xrightarrow{\sim} i^*f^*$ by the pullback compositor for $jf'$, the equality $jf'=fi$, and the pullback compositor for $fi$. Define the underived restriction mate $\beta:j^*f_*\to f'_*i^*$ as the mate of $\chi$ under $f^*\dashv f_*$ and $f'^*\dashv f'_*$. Define $D\chi:D(f'^*)D(j^*)\xrightarrow{\sim}D(i^*)D(f^*)$ by applying the exact termwise derived functor to $\chi$ and inserting the canonical comparisons for derived composites. Define $\rho:D(j^*)Rf_*\to Rf'_*D(i^*)$ to be its mate under the exact-left derived adjunctions $D(f^*)\dashv Rf_*$ and $D(f'^*)\dashv Rf'_*$. These four constructions need only the commutative square, with no Cartesian, open, finite-type, or coefficient-admissibility assumption. In addition, for an open immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ [def-weil-open-immersion], $M\in\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_Y}$ and $V\to X$ in $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$, define the section coprojection $c_{j,M,V}:M(V\xrightarrow{}X\xrightarrow jY)\to(j^*M)(V)$ as follows: first apply the component at the composite $jV$ of the module adjunction unit $M\to j_*j^*M$, then restrict $(j^*M)(V\times_YX)$ along the canonical site arrow $V\to V\times_YX$, $v\mapsto(v,v\to X)$. All maps use the canonical pulled-back coefficient actions. This node defines the specified maps and comparisons; it asserts no invertibility theorem for $\beta$, $\rho$, or $c$.
